paragraphs: Longeye sells an AI-powered investigative workspace that law enforcement agencies use to analyze digital evidence. An investigator uploads video, audio, phone extractions, social media exports, financial records, and images, then asks questions in plain language. Every answer links back to the exact moment in a video, recording, message, or image, so a finding can be checked later.

Audio and video are transcribed and translated, with searchable transcripts across Spanish, Mandarin, and 99+ more. Each call then lands on a timeline color-coded by relevancy so the conversations most likely to matter come first. A map view plots GPS tracker pings, Cellebrite extraction data, CDR lat/long, and ALPR hits, with a slider that animates movement over time. A standalone product, Longeye Monitor, applies the same engine to jail call review for corrections agencies and jail facilities.

Longeye says it is deployed across the country, from major metropolitan departments and state bureaus of investigation to corrections intelligence units running jail call analysis. Chief Darrell Lowe of the Redmond Police Department is quoted crediting it with closing gaps in a cold-case homicide. On security, the company states it is SOC 2 Type II certified, isolates evidence per agency on dedicated US infrastructure, and never uses evidence to train a large language model. Longeye has raised $5M in seed funding led by Andreessen Horowitz's American Dynamism Fund.

quote.text: The truth is buried in the evidence. Longeye finds it 100x faster.
